issues.title: Authored final-standings presentation is not used at match completion
issues.issue: Completed matches provide the result only through the arena chat summary before reset. The v1.1.3 artifact contains a dedicated final-standings ActionForm, but the terminal flow never invokes it and does not emit a winning on-screen title or victory sound. Tester runtime confirms there is no dedicated winning UI after the match.
reproduction: Complete a normal Build & Decode match through the final round.
Observe the terminal presentation after the winner is determined.
Check the chat/result text and whether a dedicated winning title or final standings UI appears before the arena resets.
issues.observed: Tester runtime on v1.1.3 confirms the match ends without a dedicated winning title/final UI. Source proves that ArenaService.finish() calls game.say(game.matchSummary()), so players do receive chat text such as 'Match Finished!' and the winning score/result. GuessTheBuildUI.showFinalStandings() remains implemented but has no production caller; finish() also contains no terminal setTitle() or victory-sound call before resetArena().
issues.expected: The authored end-of-match presentation is reachable from the completed-match flow so players receive a clear terminal result before the arena resets and returns them to the lobby.
issues.resolution: After durable result settlement, route completed matches through one terminal presentation owner before reset. Reuse the settled result to show the authored final standings and/or a clear winner title/sound; do not recalculate winners in the presentation layer.
issues.technicalAnalysis: The result itself is settled and communicated through chat, so this is not a missing-result-data defect. The mismatch is presentation ownership: the artifact contains an authored final standings surface, but the terminal lifecycle only publishes matchSummary() through chat and then resets. No terminal title/sound path compensates for the disconnected final UI.

relevantCode.reason: Defines showFinalStandings() as a dedicated final standings ActionForm.
finish() settles the result, sends matchSummary() as chat, then calls resetArena() without invoking showFinalStandings().

mustPreserve: Exact-once result settlement and leaderboard persistence.
Correct team Win/Draw semantics from the canonical result.
Automatic cleanup and return to lobby after the presentation window.

issues.title: The final round still tells players that another round is coming
issues.issue: After the last playable round ends, the HUD still displays 'Next round in …' even though no next round exists and the match will finish after the countdown.
reproduction: Play through Build & Decode until the last playable round completes.
Observe the HUD immediately after the final round ends.
Check whether it displays 'Next round in …' even though the match ends when that countdown finishes.
issues.observed: Tester runtime on v1.1.3 confirms the final round still shows 'Next round'. Source proves GuessTheBuildManager.endRound() unconditionally enters round_end, sets resultsTicks, and immediately renders 'Next round in …'. The round_end tick repeats the same HUD. Only after that countdown does ArenaService.prepareRound() call selectRound(); when no builder/word remains, selectRound() returns false and finish() ends the match.
issues.expected: When the completed round is the final playable round, the transition UI communicates match completion instead of promising another round.
issues.resolution: Resolve whether another playable round exists before publishing the round-end transition label. Keep the normal countdown for non-terminal rounds, but use terminal/match-complete messaging for the final round and hand off to the final-result presentation.
issues.technicalAnalysis: The misleading UI is caused by transition ordering. The code publishes a generic next-round countdown before terminal eligibility is resolved. Terminal detection occurs later in prepareRound() through selectRound() === false, so the final round temporarily presents a transition that cannot occur.

relevantCode.reason: endRound() and the round_end tick unconditionally render 'Next round in …' for every completed round.
prepareRound() only determines after the countdown that selectRound() is false and then calls finish().

mustPreserve: Normal between-round countdown timing for non-terminal rounds.

devNotes.title: Anti-Cheat Protection Is Not Registered in Production
devNotes.problem: AntiCheatManager still defines Creative/Spectator correction for non-admin players, but the v1.1.3 production bootstrap does not import or instantiate it. The current lobby owner now independently normalizes ordinary participants to Adventure, so this module is dead/overlapping protection rather than evidence that lobby role normalization is missing.
devNotes.action: Decide whether AntiCheatManager remains an intended defense-in-depth owner. If not, remove the dead module; if it is required, register it without duplicating the active ArenaService role policy.

evidence.finding: v1.1.3 main.js still does not register AntiCheatManager, while ArenaService.normalizeLobbyRole() now sets ordinary lobby participants to Adventure and disables mayfly.

devNotes.title: Correct the Daylight-Cycle GameRules Property Name
devNotes.problem: Build & Decode intends to keep daylight cycling disabled. In v1.1.3, WorldData still uses the key doDaylightCycle while the @minecraft/server GameRules property is doDayLightCycle, so the setup code does not reliably own/reassert that rule if world state changes later.
devNotes.action: Correct the existing WorldData/WorldManager gamerule key to doDayLightCycle and keep the same world-setup owner. Do not create a second gamerule authority.

devNotes.title: Temporary Debug Picker Is Still Included in Release
devNotes.problem: The v1.1.3 production entrypoint imports scripts/dev/debug-stick.js on every world load. The module identifies itself as a standalone temporary coordinate picker and registers block-interaction and script-event diagnostics. Its interactive paths are explicitly admin-gated, so current selected-artifact evidence does not justify a gameplay BUG.
devNotes.action: Remove the temporary debug picker from the production bootstrap when it is no longer required, or make its release inclusion an explicit maintained developer capability. Keep the existing explicit admin permission gate if the tool remains shipped.

evidence.finding: main.js imports ./dev/debug-stick.js unconditionally. The module calls itself a temporary coordinate picker and registers interaction/status/export diagnostics; all actionable paths check PermissionData.isAdmin(player).

devNotes.title: Entity Setup Script Event Has No Explicit Permission Gate
devNotes.problem: SetupManager handles the setup:entity script event by killing and respawning configured setup entities, but the handler does not check the source against the canonical PermissionData admin owner. Current selected-artifact evidence proves the missing explicit gate, but does not prove that an ordinary player can invoke the script event in the delivered runtime.
devNotes.action: Route setup:entity through the existing admin permission owner before mutating world entities. Do not rely on implicit command/runtime reachability as the only privilege boundary.

evidence.finding: SetupManager subscribes to scriptEventReceive and executes setupEntities(event.sourceEntity) for setup:entity without PermissionData.isAdmin or another explicit permission check.

devNotes.title: Player Initialization Properties Are Written but Never Consumed
devNotes.problem: WelcomeManager writes one world dynamic property named player_<scoreboardParticipantId> containing player name/id data for initialized players. The v1.1.3 production scripts contain no reader or cleanup path for those properties, so the records persist as orphaned per-player state.
devNotes.action: Remove the unused player_<participantId> persistence if it has no release purpose, or give it one explicit reader and lifecycle owner with bounded cleanup. Do not keep write-only per-player world properties indefinitely.

evidence.finding: savePlayerData() writes player_<participantId>. Full production-script search finds no getDynamicProperty/read path for that namespace and no deletion path.

devNotes.title: Legacy Capacity and Timing Config Is Still Shipped but Unused
devNotes.problem: GuessTheBuildData still declares minPlayers, maxPlayers, roundStartCountdown, and lobby.waitingTime, while v1.1.3 runtime admission and timing use ArenaConfig.RULES. Full production-script search finds no consumer for those GameData fields.
devNotes.action: Remove the unused GameData capacity/timing declarations or route the active gameplay owner through one canonical configuration source. Keep one editable authority for each capacity/timing concept.

evidence.finding: GameData.minPlayers/maxPlayers/roundStartCountdown/lobby.waitingTime have no production consumers; RULES.minPlayers/maxPlayers and active arena countdown owners are used instead.
